nodes.label: ℛ — the reconstruction/closure operator
E(X) — the external definition cost
nodes.rationale: E measures what an index costs to specify beyond its own coordinates; E = 0 means the constraints are the index.

nodes.rationale: Greedy removal gave 12/11/12 and the section once read 'at most ten'; branch and bound gave seven exactly, which is the failure protocol §2.24 earned.

The law of realised closure (§18.4.1)
nodes.rationale: Restated in certificate form because its first form had no falsifier: 'realised' was never given a test, so the law could only be confirmed by naming and never refuted.

nodes.label: The certificate as realiser
nodes.rationale: A certificate is checkable where a search is not — 362 comparisons against eight and a half million, and brute force cannot reach Janet at all.

nodes.label: E(X) is the prediction budget
nodes.rationale: An index may be complete or predictive, never both: a prediction is a proposal about an unlisted cell, and completeness is the property of having none.

nodes.label: The periodic table — E(X) = 36
The Janet left-step table — E = 0
Helium's placement, and what it costs
nodes.rationale: E is a property of where helium is drawn, not of the elements: group 18 gives 36, group 2 gives 20, a difference of sixteen cells.

nodes.label: The calendar — E = 7, the content of 'Thirty days hath September'
nodes.rationale: Non-closure is a purchase rather than a fault: E = 7 is the price of keeping January first, and the repaired calendar is unusable.

nodes.label: The measured nuclide chart — E = 9
nodes.rationale: The drawn band closes necessarily because ℛ is idempotent; reporting a band's closure as a finding about nuclei put a tautology in the same column as a measurement.

nodes.label: First ionization energies — four refused steps

Λ is distributive
Rank is conserved — modularity, exact
nodes.rationale: The question came from celestial mechanics, which is organised around invariants; a spectroscopist would not think to ask what Λ conserves.

nodes.label: Sperner, and not rank-symmetric

Order dimension exactly 8
nodes.rationale: Asserted rather than derived until the dependency graph of the book's mathematics was built and looked at for objects nothing derives; it follows from Dilworth on the seventeen generators.

nodes.rationale: d(x,x)=1 is not a convention: a point has no volume but it is one point, and the measure counts occupied cells.

nodes.rationale: A tree has no cycles for inclusion–exclusion to correct, so an index whose constraint graph is a tree has its void in closed form.

nodes.rationale: Available: AND, OR, implication. Absent: NOT, feedback, memory — so it decides membership and does not compute a function of successive inputs.

The shape — a cylinder over the transfer
Time as an order, not a stamp
nodes.rationale: A transition is a type and types are not dated; what enters is composition — a predecessor and a successor — and occupancy never rises along it.

nodes.rationale: P22's 'no lie can exist within it' is false — a forged index still closes; what a complete index converts is deception into disagreement, since every rule is content rather than inference.

nodes.label: The principles P1–P23

The twenty-five prime audits
nodes.rationale: An audit that reads the wrong artefact will pass anything: twenty-eight cross-references and 107 blank operator boxes passed clean because every audit read the source and none read the page.

nodes.rationale: Strictly stronger than closure: Λ has had E = 0 since Chapter 7 and has never had Q = ∅, because closure is about what an index holds and completeness about what it has been asked.
